home.why.title: Why Sahla?
home.why.sub: Sahla means “easy” in Moroccan Arabic. Our job is to make Morocco easy to understand, with information you can check.
home.why.1.title: Practical information
home.why.1.text: Prices, steps, timings and documents: what you need to act, without padding.
home.why.2.title: Verifiable sources
home.why.2.text: Sensitive guides point to the relevant official body so you can check every rule.
home.why.3.title: Updated content
home.why.3.text: Each guide shows its update date, and figures that change are dated.
home.why.4.title: Built for MREs and travellers
home.why.4.text: Two audiences, two paths: going home for the summer or discovering the country.

glossary.title: Morocco administrative glossary
glossary.description: Adoul, Watiqa, CNIE, ICE, apostille, land title, TSAV, ADII, CNSS, AMO: short definitions of Moroccan administrative terms, with source and guide.
glossary.intro: The words you meet in Moroccan procedures, explained simply. Each term points to an official source and to the guide that details the procedure. Definitions are general: amounts and deadlines are in the guides, with their verification date.
glossary.note: "Official source" links lead to the organisation’s home page: look there for the relevant section. Definitions are not legal advice.
calendar.title: Morocco procedures calendar
calendar.description: Month by month: TSAV vignette, declarations, Marhaba, Ramadan, holidays, the car 180 days, school start. Dates confirmed, expected or to be confirmed.
calendar.intro: Each line has a status: "confirmed" (date read in an official source), "expected" (calculation or observed practice) or "to be confirmed" (no date published). Never rely on an expected date for a deadline: check with the organisation.
